A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000, from an error converting $0.50\text{ mm}^2$ to $\text{m}^2$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10, from a power-of-ten error in length or area conversion.

C.explanation: Follows from $x = FL/(AE)$ with SI units to give $3.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}$.

D.explanation: Too large by a factor of 100, from using $0.50\text{ mm}^2$ without converting to $\text{m}^2$ correctly.

hints: Convert the given $300\text{ cm}$ to metres and $0.50\text{ mm}^2$ to $\text{m}^2$ using $1\text{ mm}^2 = 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2$.
Recall Young modulus as $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain} = FL/(Ax)$, where $F = 10\text{ N}$ is the load.
Rearrange to $x = FL/(AE)$, substitute $L = 3.0\text{ m}$, $A = 5.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^2$ and $E = 2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ Pa}$, then simplify the powers of 10.
walkthrough: Convert to SI units: length $L = 300\text{ cm} = 3.0\text{ m}$ and area $A = 0.50\text{ mm}^2 = 0.50 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2 = 5.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^2$.
State the Young modulus relation: $E = (F/A)/(x/L)$, so $E = FL/(Ax)$.
Substitute with units: $x = (10\text{ N})(3.0\text{ m})/[(5.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^2)(2.0 \times 10^{11}\text{ Pa})]$.
Evaluate extension: $x = 30/1.0 \times 10^{5} = 3.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}$, with unit metres as required. This is option C.
